title: The Technical Scope Forum Post is the only link binding an off-chain audit to the on-chain bytecode
content:
The Forum Post requirements at A.1.10.2.3.2.1.2.1.2.1 include "a link to the audit reports... hosted on the auditor's website or another independently verifiable source," "confirmation that the deployed code matches the commit hash that was sent for audit," and that "constructor arguments are as expected in the Init script."

Each of those is an assertion made in prose by the team that wrote and deployed the module. An audit certifies a *commit*; a chain holds *bytecode*; and the only thing joining them in this process is a claim in a forum thread. Constructor arguments are the sharper case — they are not covered by the audit at all, yet they determine the module's live configuration.

The Atlas is aware of the exposure and answers it socially rather than technically: A.1.10.2.3.2.1.2.1.2 requires that "the Spell Team not involved in the technical Forum Post creation must confirm the contents of the Forum Post as a public reply to ensure transparency and independent verification."

That is a genuine control, but it is second-party attestation, not verification by construction. Anyone auditing the process should treat the commit-hash-to-bytecode step as the seam where a compromise would be hardest to detect after the fact, because a false attestation here is indistinguishable from a true one without independently rebuilding the artifact.
description: A.1.10.2.3.2.1.2.1.2.1 requires a human attestation that deployed code matches the audited commit hash and that constructor args match the Init script — nothing automated enforces either.
